info.title: Starter API
info.description:
## Introduction Welcome to the **API Documentation**. This API provides a set of endpoints to help you integrate its features into your application efficiently. --- **SDKs Available** To simplify integration, we offer SDKs for popular programming languages: - [Node.js SDK](#) ---
## Authentication The API uses **Bearer Token** for authentication. All protected requests must include an `Authorization` header with the token: **Header Example:** ```json Authorization: Bearer ``` To obtain a token, authenticate via the `/auth` module. Tokens are valid for a specified duration and must be refreshed periodically.
---
## Filters Filters allow you to narrow down your query results by specifying conditions. Use query parameters to apply filters. **Example Request:** ```json GET /resource?category=books&status=ACTIVE ``` This example fetches resources filtered by `category=books` and `status=ACTIVE`. **Filter Field** Some endpoints provide a special field called `filter`, which allows for advanced filtering using an **OR** logic. This can be useful for querying multiple conditions on specified fields. The fields available for the `filter` parameter will be defined by the specific endpoint. **Example Request with Filter Field:** ```json GET /resource?filter=Harry Potter ``` In this example, the API applies the `filter` parameter across a static set of fields (e.g., `title`, `description`, and `author`) to retrieve resources that match "Harry Potter" in any of those fields.
---
## Pagination The API supports pagination to manage large sets of data efficiently. Use the `offset` and `limit` query parameters to specify which part of the dataset you want to retrieve. **How It Works** - **`offset`**: Defines the starting point of the data subset. The first item is at `offset=0`. - **`limit`**: Specifies the maximum number of items to return in the response. **Example Request:** ```json GET /resource?offset=0&limit=10 ``` This example retrieves the first 10 items from the dataset. **Pagination Response Format:** ```json { "values": [...], "meta": { "total": 100, "offset": 0, "limit": 10, } } ``` **Notes:** - **`total`**: The total number of items in the dataset. - **`offset`**: The starting position of the current subset. - **`limit`**: The number of items returned in this request. This approach ensures efficient data retrieval while giving developers fine-grained control over paginated responses.
---
## Fields The `fields` parameter allows you to specify which fields should be included in the response. This helps reduce the payload size by excluding unnecessary data, making your requests more efficient. **How It Works** By using the `fields` parameter, you can define a comma-separated list of fields you want to include in the response. **Example Request:** ```json GET /resource?fields=name,email,phone ``` In this example, the API will only include the `name`, `email`, and `phone` fields in the response. **Example Response:** ```json { "name": "John Doe", "email": "johndoe@example.com", "phone": "+123456789" } ``` **Notes:** - If the `fields` parameter is omitted, the API will return all available fields by default. - Specifying invalid or unsupported field names will result in those fields being ignored, but the request will still succeed. - Nested fields are supported (e.g., `fields=address.city`). **Benefits of Using Fields:** - **Performance:** Reduces the size of the response payload, speeding up data transfer. - **Clarity:** Returns only the data relevant to your application. This feature is ideal for optimizing API responses in applications where only specific data points are needed.
---
## Error The API uses standardized error responses to ensure consistency and make error handling easier for developers. All errors follow a consistent structure: | **Field** | **Description** | **Example** | | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------- | | `statusCode` | The HTTP status code for the error. | `400`, `404` | | `error` | A short description of the error type. | `Bad Request Error` | | `message` | A detailed message explaining what caused the error. | `Invalid input` | | `issues` (optional) | An array of key-value pairs providing details about specific issues in the request. | `[{"email": "Required"}]` | **Error Response Format** ```json { "statusCode": 400, "error": "Bad Request Error", "message": "Invalid input", "issues": [ { "email": "Required" } ] } ```
